subject: AWS Marketplace: offer display, terms and sample usage — review
messages:
From: Emily Zhou <e.zhou@acmeanalytics.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ops@acmeanalytics.com
Date: 2026-11-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Draft AWS offer content from Acme — please confirm

Hi Tessa / Lauren,

Thanks for taking a look. Attached is the first-pass of the AWS offer copy and our suggested pricing footnotes (acme-aws-offer-draft-v1.pdf, acme-pricing-footnotes.xlsx). Key asks from our side:

- Can Redwood confirm the exact UI headline length limits for the product title and short description? We want to avoid truncation.
- We included three usage examples (small-team proof-of-concept, embedded analytics for mid-market, and high-volume batch scoring). Are these the right examples for Marketplace customers?
- Pricing footnote: we referenced "per inference unit" — need guidance if Marketplace SKU should be per-API-call or per-token equivalent.
- Any co-sell language we should include to make the listing easier for AWS field (e.g., one-line partner pitch)?

We have a short security requirement from procurement (minimum retention settings, SOC2 link) referenced in the doc — we can attach evidence if you need it. We are aiming to submit to the catalog by Friday (11/13) if we can get a quick round of edits.

Attachments: acme-aws-offer-draft-v1.pdf (offer copy + hero), acme-pricing-footnotes.xlsx (footnotes and SKU mapping)

Appreciate any notes,
Emily
Emily Zhou
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme Analytics

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Emily Zhou <e.zhou@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-07T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft AWS offer content from Acme — please confirm

Emily — thanks for sending this over. Quick pass attached (see inline below) and a few actionable items so we can get the listing submitted on your timeline.

High-level: Nice structure. Hero needs to be tighter for the marketplace UI — 80 characters or less recommended for the title, 160 for the short description. Use the hero to call out one measurable benefit (e.g., "Reduce model inference cost by 40% for analytics workloads").

Usage examples: Keep the three you have but rephrase them into customer-oriented outcomes ("Prototype analytics in 2 weeks", "Embed insights for 100k users/day"). Those read better on the marketplace product page.

Pricing footnotes: Marketplace prefers concrete units. Recommend mapping to: "per 1,000 inferences" as the SKU and then including a per-token-equivalent note for customers who measure that way. Ben, see pricing notes below — can you confirm?

Co-sell one-liner: Suggest "Redwood + Acme Analytics: scalable, low-latency inference for analytics teams" (this is AWS-facing and concise). Include a single bullet about typical deal sizes/regions for the AWS field (helps prioritization).

Compliance: we can attach the SOC 2 summary in the listing assets. If you want us to host a short evidence bundle in a shared Drive link, we can add it.

Please see inline comments in the attached PDF. If these edits look good, I'll prepare the catalog submission form and share the AWS seller account steps. Can you confirm pricing SKU choice by EOD?

Thanks — t

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-07T13:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft AWS offer content from Acme — please confirm

Adding a few notes on pricing & SKU mapping (inline):

- Strongly prefer discrete SKUs that map to an objective unit: we recommend "per 1,000 inferences" for the public SKU and a private-offer priced SKU that can be quoted per month or per-commit.
- Footnote language should call out rounding and minimums: e.g., "Pricing rounded to nearest 1,000 inferences; minimum monthly commit may apply for Private Offers."
- For enterprise customers who measure tokens, include a conversion table in the footnotes rather than relying on the product description.

UI/display: agree with Tessa on character limits. Also flag the hero image — marketplace often crops to 16:9 at small sizes; confirm you have a 1200x675 JPEG version.

For co-sell: include a one-line "what the AWS seller says" blurb and a suggested contact (Sales/AE) so sellers can route leads.

I'll compile a final pricing-footnote snippet and push to the Drive link (acme-pricing-footnotes.xlsx) by 3pm PST.

- Ben

From: Emily Zhou <e.zhou@acmeanalytics.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, ops@acmeanalytics.com
Date: 2026-11-07T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft AWS offer content from Acme — please confirm

Thanks Tessa / Ben — very helpful.

Attachments: I uploaded a revised offer PDF and the updated pricing workbook to the Drive folder (links above). We switched the SKU to "per 1,000 inferences" and added the conversion table Ben suggested. Emily (procurement) attached the SOC 2 summary to the folder as well.

We can accept the suggested hero line and tightened short description — please use the suggested headline edit from Tessa in the PDF.

Next step: Tessa, can you submit the catalog form on your side and loop in AWS seller contacts? If it helps, we're available for a 20-minute review tomorrow at 10:00am PT.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Emily
